title: Outside the Closed World: On Using Machine Learning for Network Intrusion Detection
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy 2010
algorithm_class: ML-based network intrusion detection with controlled feature/label variation across environments
supported_guarantee: Empirical demonstration (Sommer & Paxson, IEEE S&P 2010) that ML intrusion detectors degrade sharply under cross-environment (cross-site/cross-traffic) evaluation, that attack-category training labels inflate apparent accuracy, and that training-data staleness costs are systematically underestimated.
limitations_vs_candidate: Warns about the exact failure mode the candidate must survive - environmental memorization and unrealistic labels - but provides no detector, no multi-tenant agent telemetry, no false-positive-budget endpoint and no authorization-boundary semantics; it is a critique/measurements paper, not a runnable detection baseline for agent events.
mechanism_analysis: Claim-matrix C5 methodological anchor: the paper's core finding - detectors memorize their training environment and labels leak - is the reason the DIMVA protocol freezes cross-family/cross-tenant holdouts and masks rejection reason codes in the primary leak-safe test; if the masked-vs-unmasked ablation and family holdout leave all arms statistically unchanged within the preregistered margin, this premise is refuted and masking must be justified on privacy grounds alone (novelty contract C5 falsification). It is not an executable comparator: no official implementation release exists to pin, so the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN, and its role is to govern evaluation design, never to serve as a scored arm.

title: Static threshold on denied-request counts per sliding window (blueprint arm B0; registry baseline static-threshold-denied-per-window)
algorithm_class: Counting detector: alarm when denied/failed request count in a fixed sliding window exceeds a tuned threshold
supported_guarantee: Strong operational baseline and RQ1's strongest competing explanation: counting alone is what a SOC would deploy first, so any campaign detector must beat this trivial counter on leak-safe features (no rejection reason codes) at the preregistered false-alarm budget per 1000 benign sessions.
limitations_vs_candidate: A fixed-window count is structurally blind to order, pacing and linkage: a low-and-slow campaign paced under the window (DIMVA-CASE-03/05) produces the same per-window count as benign retry bursts and outage backlogs, and purpose-hopping or permission-discovery chains (DIMVA-CASE-02/07) with individually-justified requests can stay under any threshold; no campaign-intent notion exists.
mechanism_analysis: RQ1 primary falsification arm (novelty contract: if B0 matches the candidate's campaign AUCPR within margin delta at the fixed false-positive budget on the leak-safe split, no sequence-modeling necessity is claimed): the registry entry (parity fixture evaluation/venue2027/dimva/fixtures/threshold_parity.json, exec_command registered) defines threshold-on-denied-counts with leak-safe features only, but the implementation does not exist in this worktree (evaluation/venue2027 absent), so it is honestly UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN rather than scored; the falsification rule applies at full strength once the parity fixture lands.

title: Temporal rule sequence / finite-state signature detector (blueprint arm B1; registry baseline temporal-rule-sequence-signature)
algorithm_class: Deterministic finite-state alarm detector: hand-authored rule sequence / event-kind signature matching over ordered minimal-event sequences with no learned parameters
supported_guarantee: Strong interpretable detection baseline and RQ3's strongest competing explanation: ordered signature matching over the minimal event schema (event kind, scoped actor/tenant/purpose, logical time, digest refs) alarms exactly on the multi-step patterns (purpose hop then receipt reuse) that a pure counter misses, while remaining fully auditable by operators.
limitations_vs_candidate: Hand-authored signatures are tuned to one environment's event vocabulary and pacing: tool renames/re-binds, interleaved benign traffic and inter-arrival shifts beyond the tuned window (A3/A4 capabilities in threat_model.md) defeat them - precisely the environmental-memorization risk sommer10 documents; unseen-family (DIMVA-CASE-07) recall is undefined for signatures never written.
mechanism_analysis: RQ3 pacing-robustness reference (novelty contract: B1 is the strongest competing explanation for any apparent adaptive-robustness gain, and rule arms B0/B1 matching sequence models on family-held-out traces kills the ML-necessity claim): registry entry (parity fixture evaluation/venue2027/dimva/fixtures/rule_sequence_parity.json) declares a leak-safe FSM signature baseline, but the in-project implementation does not exist yet in this worktree, so UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN is recorded; the arm must be built faithfully or reported NOT_RUN_EXTERNAL, never replaced by a toy under the same name (execution contract rule 8).

title: Isolation Forest on privacy-minimized counts (blueprint arm B2; registry baseline isolation-forest-privacy-minimized)
algorithm_class: Unsupervised anomaly detection: sklearn.ensemble.IsolationForest over privacy-minimized per-window feature counts
supported_guarantee: Executable unsupervised comparator requiring no labels: scikit-learn's IsolationForest (pinned tag 1.8.0, tag object 63acddb6de687f685b7323ad68fb2cf76cc3bd1a -> commit 646da0f072a8afef6a980aa427a710311e67eb9d, verified live via GitHub API 2026-11-15; registry entry isolation-forest-privacy-minimized, ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM) isolates outliers on leak-safe features with random_state pinned.
limitations_vs_candidate: Isolation Forest scores per-window feature vectors, not linked event campaigns: it has no sequence order, no campaign-intent state and no purpose-transition semantics, and its unsupervised thresholding gives no principled control at a preregistered false-alarm budget; cross-family degradation is expected but its anomaly scores are not campaign-level probabilities.
mechanism_analysis: RQ2 unsupervised comparator (blueprint arm B2): the registry pins actual scikit-learn 1.8.0 upstream (tag-object dereference verified 2026-11-15, BSD-3-Clause) running sklearn.ensemble.IsolationForest on privacy-minimized counts with family-held-out evaluation; if an unsupervised count-based anomaly score matches the candidate's campaign AUCPR on the family-held-out leak-safe split at the fixed budget, the sequence-modeling claim collapses to 'any outlier detector suffices' and the paper reports that negative result instead of ML necessity.

title: Gradient-boosted trees on controlled leak-safe features (blueprint arm B3; registry baseline gradient-boosted-trees-controlled-features)
algorithm_class: Supervised gradient-boosted decision trees: sklearn.ensemble.HistGradientBoostingClassifier over a controlled feature set
supported_guarantee: Strongest supervised comparator for RQ2: scikit-learn's HistGradientBoostingClassifier (pinned tag 1.8.0, commit 646da0f072a8afef6a980aa427a710311e67eb9d, verified live 2026-11-15; registry entry gradient-boosted-trees-controlled-features, ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM) learns nonlinear feature interactions from leak-safe labeled windows with random_state pinned.
limitations_vs_candidate: Window-level supervised scoring still aggregates events into feature vectors: temporal order inside a window is discarded, cross-window campaigns must be linked by an external scheme, and - per sommer10 - supervised labels on synthetic traces risk inflating in-distribution accuracy that evaporates on the frozen unseen-family holdout (DIMVA-CASE-06/07).
mechanism_analysis: RQ2 strongest supervised baseline (novelty contract: B3 is the comparator the generalization claim must beat): the registry pins actual scikit-learn 1.8.0 with controlled leak-safe features (no rejection reason codes) and family-held-out splits; the candidate may claim temporal-model necessity only if it beats B3 on held-out-family recall and AUCPR within the preregistered statistics plan - otherwise the negative result is reported and no ML-necessity claim is made.

title: Sequence model with time-aware features over the minimal event schema (blueprint arm B4; candidate family, not an external comparator)
algorithm_class: Candidate: time-aware sequence model over the minimal event schema (event kind, scoped actor/tenant/purpose, logical time, payload digest references) with rejection reason codes masked in the primary leak-safe test
supported_guarantee: Prospective design commitment (not yet demonstrated): linking individually-justified requests into multi-step probing campaigns - purpose hopping, receipt/lineage reuse, permission-discovery chains - and detecting them at a preregistered fixed false-alarm budget with unseen-family generalization; admitted as the candidate only if it shows holdout gain over B0-B3.
limitations_vs_candidate: It is the candidate itself, not a comparator: until the candidate implementation lands no artifact exists, no run_id manifest exists, and every guarantee here is a prospective design commitment per the frozen novelty contract - this row makes the candidate auditable against B0-B3 and never asserts results.
mechanism_analysis: Candidate arm B4 recorded for falsification transparency (novelty contract strong-baseline set: 'candidate; only if holdout gain'): the mechanism - campaign-level linkage over minimal events with masked reason codes and cross-family holdout - is exactly what RQ1-RQ3 measure against B0-B3; until the candidate exists in evaluation/venue2027/dimva the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN, and if B0/B1 match it on family-held-out traces or its performance depends on unmasked reason-code labels, the ML-necessity claim is refused and the primary experiment invalidated per the falsification rules.

title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
algorithm_class: Stateful prompt-injection attack/defense benchmark for tool-integrated LLM agents with executable task suites
supported_guarantee: Executable adversarial task suites (Debenedetti et al., NeurIPS 2024 D&B) measuring whether agents complete tasks under active injection; pinned tag v0.1.35 (commit a75aba7631d3ca5fb7ab938965c97ead2f9ff84b, MIT, verified live via GitHub API 2026-11-15; registry entry agentdojo-attack-observability, ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM).
limitations_vs_candidate: Security evaluation is environment-level robustness of a single agent run: the unit is one task execution against one injection, not a multi-step campaign over an event stream - there is no authorization-boundary telemetry, no campaign-level AUCPR at a false-positive budget, no benign-retry controls and no unseen-family holdout over attack families; its oracle labels instruction compliance, not campaign intent.
mechanism_analysis: Claim-matrix C1 boundary comparator and independent-trace source (blueprint: agent safety attacks are the closest realistic corpus): the registry agentdojo-attack-observability entry uses the pinned attack suite to generate independent multi-stage traces for cross-family evaluation - so AgentDojo supplies attack realism, not the detection endpoint; if a detector derived from agentdojo24 attack traces alone reached campaign-level PR-AUC at the fixed budget on our family-held-out split, novelty contract C1 would falsify the contribution and force re-scoping. It is not executed as a scored arm in P01 (parity fixture registered for later phases), so the matrix records verified upstream code while the mechanism analysis fixes its boundary role.

title: ToolEmu: Identifying the Risks of LM Agents with an LM-Emulated Sandbox
algorithm_class: LM-emulated tool sandbox with judge-validated risk taxonomy (quantitative riskiness plus LM judge scoring)
supported_guarantee: Scalable identification and quantification of LM-agent risks: emulated tool execution with GPT-4-judged risk scoring validated against human annotators (Ruan et al., ICLR 2024); pinned HEAD ac4a7ab7ed8c7985d96231e214bd6b54304b7ddb (Apache-2.0, verified live via GitHub API 2026-11-15; registry entry toolemu-risk-emulation, ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM, venues [acns]).
limitations_vs_candidate: Emulated tool outcomes are simulated text, never persisted authorization events: there is no event collector, no multi-tenant telemetry, no benign-retry/outage controls, no false-positive-budgeted detection endpoint and no unseen-family detection holdout; the judge scores risky use cases, not authorization-boundary campaigns over time.
mechanism_analysis: Claim-matrix C2 boundary comparator (novelty contract: simulation-based risk scoring is the closest alternative to a detection study): registry entry toolemu-risk-emulation pins the upstream repo (verified 2026-11-15) but its registered venue is acns, so DIMVA records the verified code honestly while fixing the role - simulated outcomes are not persisted authorization events (registry relation); if ToolEmu-style emulation were shown to already supply an equivalent campaign-detection metric at a fixed false-positive budget with unseen-family holdout, C2 falsifies the endpoint and the claim is refused. Deliberately not executed as a scored DIMVA arm in P01.

title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
algorithm_class: Tool-agent-user interaction benchmark scoring policy-following and final database-state correctness in multi-turn dialogues
supported_guarantee: End-state correctness evaluation: an agent conversing with a simulated user must mutate a database to satisfy domain policy checks plus a pass^k chat-quality metric (Sierra et al., ICLR 2025); upstream repo live and MIT-licensed (default-branch HEAD 59a200c6d575d595120f1cb70fea53cef0632f6b verified via GitHub API 2026-11-15, no release tags exist to pin).
limitations_vs_candidate: Policy compliance is scored once on the final database state in retail/airline domains: there is no event stream, no campaign concept, no temporal detection metric, no false-alarm budget and no unseen-attack-family holdout; the registry itself warns the historical repo's tasks are outdated (ledger relation), so it is an evaluation-endpoint comparator, not a detector.
mechanism_analysis: Claim-matrix C3 boundary comparator (tau-bench is the closest published tool-agent evaluation with an independent policy oracle): the code link is registry-listed and verified live 2026-11-15, but no release tag exists (tags list empty via GitHub API), so any future run must pin the recorded HEAD; if a tau-bench-derived evaluation yielded equivalent unseen-family campaign detection at bounded false alarms, novelty contract C3 would refuse the endpoint as non-distinct. Mechanistically, pass^k over final states cannot express campaign-level AUCPR at a fixed false-positive budget - the DIMVA endpoint is temporal over event streams, which is exactly the delta this row documents.

title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
algorithm_class: Indirect prompt-injection threat taxonomy for tool-integrated LLM agents (direct/indirect harm categories)
supported_guarantee: Dataset measuring whether tool-integrated agents comply with malicious instructions hidden in tool content (Shi et al., Findings of ACL 2024): attack taxonomy covering direct-harm and data-exfiltration cases with/without data access, establishing the semantic injection threat model for tool agents.
limitations_vs_candidate: Attack surface is model-layer instruction following via embedded content: injection families are single-shot semantic threats, not multi-step authorization-boundary probing campaigns - no pacing, no purpose/epoch transitions, no receipt reuse, no minimal-event telemetry and no campaign detection metric; the corpus cannot provide benign-retry controls at a false-alarm budget.
mechanism_analysis: Claim-matrix C4 boundary comparator and holdout-split source: the registry entry injecagent-injection-taxonomy (venues [dimva]) uses its threat-family labels to structure the cross-family holdout splits only - 'taxonomy extraction only, no executable upstream revision verified' per the registry - so available_code=no reflects its registered non-execution role, and if the InjecAgent corpus plus a published detector matched the candidate's leak-safe campaign AUCPR at the fixed budget, novelty contract C4 would collapse the injection/probing boundary this study relies on. The matrix never presents it as a runnable detection arm.

title: Zanzibar: Google's Consistent, Global Authorization System
algorithm_class: Consistency-aware distributed ReBAC authorization service with zookie version tokens
supported_guarantee: Externally consistent permission evaluation at global scale: zookies bound staleness of ACL checks, per-user snapshot reads are monotonic, and tuple-change ordering is global (Pang et al., USENIX ATC 2019) - the reference verification-time authorization architecture.
limitations_vs_candidate: Consistency governs permission-tuple evaluation at decision time only: there is no telemetry stream, no event-kind schema, no campaign notion and no temporal detection endpoint - a probing campaign whose every request is individually authorized produces zero Zanzibar events to detect on, so no false-positive-budgeted campaign AUCPR can even be defined from its mechanism.
mechanism_analysis: Claim-matrix C6 boundary comparator (novelty contract: verification-time permission system with no temporal campaign-detection surface): a design paper with no official Google code release - execution of the authorization-mechanism class goes through the openfga ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM row in the shared registry - so the honest DIMVA status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN; if a published authorization platform shipped a telemetry detector evaluated at a fixed false-positive budget with unseen-family holdout equal to ours, C6 falsifies the claim. The row's role is to prove the candidate competes in a different dimension (detection over time, not admission correctness).

title: Macaroons: Cookies with Contextual Caveats for Decentralized Authorization in the Cloud
algorithm_class: HMAC caveat-chain context-bound capability credentials with first-class attenuation
supported_guarantee: Contextual caveats (actor, expiry, and application-defined predicates such as purpose) attenuate an unrestricted root identifier, verified by an HMAC chain at presentation time; delegation without key sharing; third-party caveats (Birgisson et al., NDSS 2014) - the strong token baseline of the IFIP_SEC sibling study.
limitations_vs_candidate: Caveat satisfaction is pointwise at verification time: the mechanism has no detection-over-time endpoint, no event stream, no campaign linkage and no false-alarm budget - a probing campaign built from individually-valid caveated presentations leaves no detectable trace inside the token mechanism itself, so it cannot detect (only prevent) anything.
mechanism_analysis: Claim-matrix C7 boundary comparator (novelty contract: 'if caveat-style mechanisms are demonstrated to detect - not prevent - probing campaigns from minimal events at bounded false alarms, C7 is falsified'): upstream code is the libmacaroons reference implementation (rescrv/libmacaroons, the implementation cited by the paper's authors and registry-linked via the shared IFIP_SEC lineage), verified live 2026-11-15; the row records the verified code honestly while the mechanism analysis fixes DIMVA's boundary - Macaroons belong to the prevention sibling's endpoint (replay acceptance), and any DIMVA detection claim over their presentations requires exactly the minimal-event telemetry this study introduces, never the token mechanism alone.
